newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORWAY'S FOKUS BANK PROFITS RISE 15 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: NORWAY'S FOKUS BANK PROFITS RISE 15 PERCENT.

text.p: Fokus Bank, Norway's fourth largest bank, posted first-half 1997 net profits of 301 million crowns on Thursday, up about 15 percent from the corresponding period last year.
Net interest and credit commission rose 0.8 percent to 467 million crowns while other operating income jumped nearly 30 percent to 284 million.
Operating expenses swelled 15.5 percent to 469 million.
The result fell short of market expectations.

The bank said the accounts had been charged with 35 million crowns in expenses related to a failed merger proposal to mortgage lender BNbank and a hostile takeover attempt against Fokus by Sparebankgruppen, a group of savings banks.
The bank attributed the increased expenses to extraordinary expenses in the second quarter as well as increased provisions for performance-related pay.
Net losses on loans and guarantees amounted to a gain of 18 million crowns while the corresponding figure last year was a loss of 15.3 million.
Gross non-performing loans totalled 1.45 billion crowns, an increase of 2.8 percent from the year-end. Gross non-performing loans amounted to 4.49 percent of gross lending.
Fokus Managing Director Bjarne Borgersen said he was pleased with the performance in general and especially with the income development.

"We are very satisfied with the fact that the major part of the lending growth comes within the corporate market," he said in a statement. "This shows that Fokus Bank is strengthening its position as a regional commmercial bank.

"The processes related to BNbank and Sparebankgruppen have given extraordinary expenses and will give extraordinary gains. The gain we will make from the sale of the stake in BNbank will be accounted for in the second half of this year and will exceed the costs booked in this quarter," Borgersen said.
Fokus agreed in June to sell its 10 percent stake in BNbank to Den norske Bank (DnB), paving the way for Norway's largest bank to acquire the mortgage lender.
The sale will give Fokus a profit of 41 million crowns.
